tier_reason: thekvs/cpp-serializers is a widely cited independent third-party shootout. Its public code (benchmark.cpp thrift_serialization_test, CMakeLists.txt) runs thrift-binary against protobuf and msgpack. The README gives only 'Intel Core i7', Ubuntu 16.04 and a CMake Release build, with no compiler named for the published table, so it falls short of A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the published table on the current README, which says only 'Project was tested with Clang and GCC compilers'. Build: C++14, cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (CMake's default -O3 -DNDEBUG for GCC/Clang) plus -W -Wall -Wextra from CMakeLists.txt. The README revision that published this table (commit 3015690c, 2019-03-13) said 'Project was tested with clang 5.0.0 (Ubuntu 16.04)'.
corrections.workload: Round trip (serialize then deserialize) of one in-memory record holding a vector of 1,000 int64 values and 100 copies of an 86-char string (~17 KB serialized), Thrift via TBinaryProtocolT over TMemoryBuffer; the README says each run is 1,000,000 operations, averaged over 50 runs, and reports average total time in ms (thekvs/cpp-serializers benchmark.cpp).
corrections.caveats: This is the third-party thekvs/cpp-serializers shootout from 2019 (thrift 0.12.0, protobuf 3.7.0, msgpack 3.1.1, 'Intel Core i7', Ubuntu 16.04); the current README names no compiler or exact CPU. Only the binary protocol wins: thrift-compact (3474.32 ms) is slower than both protobuf (2312.78) and msgpack (2560.6). Thrift is itself a major incumbent RPC/serialization stack. The test is a single record round-tripped through in-memory buffers, so it says nothing about RPC cost. The pre-2019 table on the same README also had thrift-binary ahead (13335 vs protobuf 24717 and msgpack 33815 ms). The implied ~1.2 us per ~17 KB round trip looks too fast for the stated 1,000,000 iterations, and the README's pre-2019 table (Core i5, Ubuntu 14.04, older library versions) showed ~11x larger totals, so the iteration label may be off; the ratios are unaffected.

notes: All numbers appear verbatim in the thekvs README table: thrift-binary 1190.22, protobuf 2312.78, msgpack 2560.6. The ratios check out (1.94x vs protobuf, 2.15x vs msgpack). gh confirms Apache-2.0, 10,960 stars, last commit 2026-09-24, not archived and not a fork. The fixes set compared_against_cpp_std_directly to false (the C++ std library has no serializer), fill in compiler/flags, make the workload more precise, and make the caveats self-contained. The repo entered known_list.txt only through this wave's merge (6ded485), so it is not a duplicate.
